originality.rationale: The full relevant theorem and bounds in the 2026 multiset study were inspected: Theorem 9 gives a general upper bound for t=n-3 only from n>=q+2, not the exact four-symbol 6/5/4 staircase for all n>=5. The published exact three-survivor published-finding corpus finding is explicitly ternary and its complete RESULT.md excludes q>=4. Neither the general polynomial-deletion-ball sequel nor the earlier lattice/simplex framework gives the observed quaternary exceptional two-light-vector compatibility classification. Actual indexed searches for multiset, discrete-simplex, L1 metric, q=4, all lengths, and numeric profile yielded no implying theorem; unindexed mathematical tables remain a specific residual priority risk.
residual_risks: Indexed semantic searches and inspected papers cannot rule out an equivalent result in unindexed short-distance discrete-simplex tables or other terminology.
The sequel full source was compared through relevant material, not a proof of coverage absence in every external version.

value.rationale: Determines a natural maximum cardinality throughout the four-symbol three-survivor high-deletion regime, beyond an already established ternary benchmark. Its 6-to-5-to-4 staircase has two nontrivial transition thresholds and a genuine extra exceptional two-light configuration at n=5; the structural mechanism distinguishes this classification from routine substitution or bare finite code search. It is useful as an exact small-alphabet benchmark for general bounds, and no downstream universal claim is needed.
